compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the seed's Blueprint/multi-file structure for a flat single-file app.py monolith; Session 4's repository refactor only partially repaired this — routes never migrated to Blueprints, leaving app.py as a growing monolith
Schema evolution relied on brittle try/except ALTER TABLE migrations (owner_id in S2, email in S3) rather than a migration framework, which is fragile across fresh vs. existing databases
The greenfield session never implemented DELETE /tasks despite the CRUD spec, and no later session backfilled it — the endpoint set stayed partial
Session 5's Flask-Limiter defaults to a Redis storage URI in production, adding a runtime infra dependency not present in earlier sessions
key_decisions: Session 1: rebuild as a flat single-file Flask app with per-request SQLite connections, dropping the seed's Blueprint/JWT/auth scaffolding entirely
Session 2: JWT auth with werkzeug password hashing plus an owner_id column providing per-user task isolation enforced at the query level
Session 2: try/except ALTER TABLE migration step to add owner_id without breaking existing data
Session 3: decouple async email notifications via Celery+Redis (celery_config.py, tasks.py), triggered only on status transition to 'completed' and mocked in tests
Session 4: extract BaseRepository ABC plus TaskRepository/UserRepository so route handlers stop touching raw SQL, keeping API behavior identical
Session 5: per-user Flask-Limiter rate limiting (token-derived key) and cursor-based pagination with next_cursor/total response format
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across the story. Session 1 delivered a minimal but fully tested flat CRUD API (13 tests); Session 2 layered JWT auth and per-user isolation on top with a data-safe migration; Session 3 integrated an async Celery notification worker without breaking existing endpoints; Session 4 was a clean, behavior-preserving repository-pattern refactor evidenced by the test suite remaining at 36 tests with zero modifications; Session 5 capped it with rate limiting and cursor pagination, pushing the suite to 46 passing tests. The code moved from a single-file monolith toward a layered architecture (routes → repositories → SQL), and each session respected prior invariants — the progression is textbook incremental software evolution with no sign of degradation.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, steadily-improving five-session build where each phase (greenfield → auth → async integration → repository refactor → cross-cutting hardening) built cleanly on the last with a monotonically growing, always-green test suite — marred only by a persistent route monolith and ad-hoc ALTER TABLE migrations.
